questions.referenceAnswer: Let u = sin(x), du = cos(x)dx. When x=0, u=0; x=pi/2, u=1. \int_0^1 u du = [u^2/2]_0^1 = 1/2.
expectedConcepts: Substitution method or double angle identity
Correct change of limits or antiderivative
markingCriteria: 3 marks for correct limits and antiderivative

questions.questionText: Prove that the area of a right-angled triangle with base b and height h is (1/2)bh. Draw labelled diagram.
questions.referenceAnswer: Complete the rectangle of sides b and h. Diagonal splits rectangle of area bh into two congruent right triangles. Area = (1/2)bh.
expectedConcepts: Labelled diagram with base b, height h, hypotenuse
acceptableAlternatives: Coordinate geometry proof placing vertices at (0,0), (b,0), (0,h)
diagramReferences: Right-angled coordinate geometry triangle with base b, height h, right angle symbol
